category_title: Students without academic skill deficits who engage in active/disruptive work avoidance
minimal_context: Martin is participating in a small-group reading activity in his second-grade classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's begin our small-group reading. Please open your books and read the next page quietly.

STUDENT: (Turns his body completely away from the assigned materials) I already know how to read. I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: Just do your best to read along with the group.

STUDENT: (Gets out of his seat and leans over to the student next to him) Hey, what are you doing after school today?

TUTOR: Martin, please sit down and focus on your book.

STUDENT: (Stays out of his seat, ignoring the book, and continues talking loudly to his peer) I don't want to read this! Did you see the new superhero movie?

options.A: Represent information in various ways by including movement and physical activity to represent reading concepts during the daily small-group instructional sessions in the second-grade classroom.
options.B: Teach the student how to choose good books for the small-group reading activities, providing explicit guidance on selecting appropriate reading materials during the daily instructional sessions.
options.C: Integrate multicultural picture books into the small-group reading activities, particularly focusing on African American stories during the daily instructional sessions in the second-grade classroom.
options.D: Meet with the student at the beginning and end of each day to review goals, allowing him to trade points for incentives such as a homework pass or stickers.
